answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring every identity to a time-locked work bond that vests slowly: a newborn agent may only take one small job per epoch, and its quota grows only after peers attest its completed work. Splitting one bond across a hundred fake identities leaves each at the dawn of its voyage with the same tiny quota, so a sybil army earns no more than a single honest agent per unit of capital, while genuine agents compound reputation and throughput epoch by epoch.
